body:
## Can you get implants after bone loss?

Often, yes. Bone loss was once a firm barrier to dental implants, but modern 3D imaging and bone augmentation techniques now make implants possible for many patients who were previously told they were not candidates. This guide from Dr. Neda Moezzi at Valencia Smile Expert explains candidacy, the diagnostic steps, augmentation options, comparative results, realistic costs, and what to ask at your consultation in Valencia. If you would like a focused evaluation, start with our [dental implants service page](/services/dental-implants/).

## Why bone matters for implants

An implant replaces a tooth root and relies on enough jawbone for stability. When bone volume or quality is low, placing an implant without preparation raises the risk of early failure and long-term problems such as implant mobility or peri-implantitis (infection and bone loss around the implant). Age alone is not the deciding factor: studies report implant survival in the high 80s to mid 90s percent at five to ten years when patients are well selected and managed. Clinical reviews consistently point to medical control and peri-implant care as stronger predictors of success than chronological age.

## How we evaluate bone loss

Diagnosis starts with a cone beam CT scan (CBCT) and a clinical exam. CBCT shows bone height and width in three dimensions and the position of critical structures such as the nerve in the lower jaw and the maxillary sinus in the upper jaw. Dr. Moezzi documents measurable deficits, any periodontal disease and the quality of the soft tissue. That data determines whether you need bone grafting, a sinus lift, short implants or another strategy.

### Key diagnostic questions

- How many millimeters of vertical bone are present at the planned site?
- Is the ridge wide enough for the planned implant diameter?
- Is the maxillary sinus enlarged near the site?
- Is there active periodontal disease or a systemic condition that slows healing?

## Treatment options when bone is limited

Several practical approaches exist. The choice depends on the size of the defect, your health, your functional goals and your budget.

- **Localized bone grafting:** socket preservation or ridge augmentation rebuilds lost bone at a single site. Graft material may be your own bone, donor bone, animal-derived bone or synthetic. Success rates are high when infection is absent and aftercare instructions are followed. For recovery expectations, see our guide on [bone grafting and pain](/bone-grafting-is-it-painful/).
- **Sinus lift (maxillary sinus augmentation):** when the upper back jaw lacks vertical height, a sinus lift creates room for graft material beneath the sinus membrane so an implant can be placed.
- **Short or narrow-diameter implants:** newer implant designs can sometimes be placed in limited bone without grafting, reducing surgery for medically complex patients.
- **Zygomatic or pterygoid implants:** for severe upper-jaw bone loss, these longer implants anchor in other facial bones and are used in full-arch reconstructions by experienced teams.
- **Implant-supported overdentures:** two to four implants stabilize a denture, often with less bone than a full fixed bridge requires, and at lower cost.

## Comparing augmentation and alternatives

| Option | When used | Recovery | Typical cost range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Localized bone graft | Single-site ridge deficiency | 1–4 weeks of soft-tissue healing; months for bone integration | $500–$3,000 depending on graft type and extent |
| Sinus lift | Upper back sites with low vertical height | 2–6 weeks soft-tissue healing; 4–9 months before the implant in some protocols | $1,500–$6,000 extra per site depending on technique |
| Short implants | Limited vertical bone where grafting is undesirable | Faster placement and shorter timeline (3–6 months healing) | $3,000–$6,000 per implant with crown |
| Implant-retained overdenture | Multiple missing teeth, limited budget | Moderate; fewer implants means less surgery | $6,000–$20,000 depending on arches and implant count |

These are typical national ranges, not the practice's fees; your written estimate will reflect your case.

## Success rates and risks after grafting

Systematic reviews show that when grafting is done properly and systemic risks are managed, implant survival remains high. Reported figures are about **90 to 98 percent at five years** and roughly **85 to 95 percent at ten years** under controlled conditions. Peri-implantitis rates vary across studies, from **5 to 20 percent**, with higher risk in patients with a history of periodontal disease. Strict hygiene and regular maintenance matter.

## Cost realities and financing

Cost is the most common barrier patients mention. Typical per-implant pricing runs **$3,000 to $6,000**, and full-arch reconstructions often exceed **$20,000**. For many older patients, an implant-supported overdenture offers the best balance of improved chewing and lower total cost. Ask for a written plan with staged options. Valencia Smile Expert accepts most major PPO plans and offers flexible financing. Our [implant cost guide](/dental-implants-valencia-cost-guide/) covers typical scenarios in more detail.

Patients who regain stable chewing after years with a loose denture often report eating a wider range of foods and feeling more confident socially, which fits the published evidence on nutrition and quality of life when the implant solution matches a patient's health and goals.

## What to ask at your consultation

- Do I need bone grafting, or can a short implant be used?
- What graft material do you recommend, and why?
- Can treatment be staged to spread cost and reduce surgical risk?
- What follow-up schedule do you recommend to prevent peri-implantitis?
- How will you coordinate with my physician if I have diabetes, heart disease or take bisphosphonates?

## Graft now, or choose a different prosthesis?

| Goal | Graft plus implant | Overdenture | Conventional denture |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stability and chewing | High | Moderate to high | Low |
| Cost | Higher | Moderate | Lower |
| Surgical complexity | Higher | Moderate | None |
| Long-term maintenance | High but durable | Moderate; attachments need upkeep | Frequent relines |

## Considerations for Valencia patients

Smoking, uncontrolled diabetes and certain medications increase the risk of graft failure and peri-implant complications. Dr. Moezzi coordinates with your primary care provider to get medical conditions under control before surgery, which lowers complication risk. The office has 3D CBCT imaging and guided implant surgery on site, along with PRF (platelet-rich fibrin) therapy, which uses your own blood components and can support healing.

## Next step

Modern imaging and a range of augmentation strategies let us tailor treatment to your health, goals and budget. If you are in Valencia or Santa Clarita, start with a CBCT-based consultation and, where needed, medical clearance, so we can determine whether grafting, short implants or an overdenture is the right path. Book an evaluation through our [dental implants service page](/services/dental-implants/) or call (661) 254-5200; we will review costs, timelines and staged options with you.

faq.q: Can I get dental implants with bone loss without bone grafting?
faq.a: Sometimes. If the deficit is small, short or narrow-diameter implants may be placed without grafting. Implant-retained overdentures also need fewer implants and can work with less bone. A CBCT scan shows whether grafting can be avoided.

faq.q: How long does bone grafting add to the implant timeline?
faq.a: Grafting typically adds two to six months before implant placement, depending on the graft type and site. In some cases the graft and implant are placed at the same visit when stability allows, which shortens the overall timeline.

faq.q: What are the success rates for implants placed after grafting?
faq.a: In medically stable patients with proper technique, studies report implant survival after grafting in the high 80s to mid 90s percent at five to ten years. Hygiene, medical control and regular maintenance are the main factors.

faq.q: Does Medicare or insurance cover bone grafts and implants?
faq.a: Medicare typically does not cover routine dental implants or grafting. Some dental plans provide partial benefits, but coverage varies. Staged treatment and financing can spread the cost; ask for a written estimate and financing options at your consultation.

faq.q: What are the signs that a graft or implant is failing?
faq.a: Increasing pain, swelling, persistent drainage, a loose implant or a change in your bite are warning signs. Early evaluation allows many situations to be salvaged, so call promptly if you notice them.

faq.q: Are implants with bone grafts painful for seniors?
faq.a: Discomfort is usually manageable with local anesthesia and modern pain-control protocols. It typically peaks in the first 48 to 72 hours and improves from there. We use layered pain control and clear recovery instructions.
